newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs said good EMU protection trades.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs said good EMU protection trades.

text.p: Belgian government bonds (OLOs) are good EMU protection trades since risks are biased towards further overperformance despite the fact that spreads are tight at current levels, JP Morgan said in its latest Markets Outlook.
"The traditional calm of July and August, and the small number of (OLO) auctions during this period, should be supportive of the Belgian market," analyst Laurent Fransolet said.
Belgians, who themselves hold a vast majority of OLOs, traditionally take their summer holidays in July and August. They are also typically reluctant to sell their holdings.
JP Morgan noted the only downside risk for OLOs would be if a crisis developed about which countries are able to qualify for Europe's single currency project.
Such a crisis, however, would not involve Belgium. This year and next the country would have no problem in reaching the three percent deficit/GDP ratio set out in the Maastricht Treaty.
JP Morgan also saw no threats to the stability of the government. "Political problems are kept under wraps by Prime Minister (Jean-Luc) Dehaene," it said.

On German government bonds (Bunds), a key directional indicator for OLOs, JP Morgan's Gottfried Hoerich said 10-year yields could ease to 5.50 percent, driven by favourable carry and a lack of bearish economic releases.
"Medium-term, however, we remain bearish on the long end with a target of six percent by September," he said.
